WILD ANIMALS AS PETS - part 1 - pet trade

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tiger cubs as pets, exotic creatures big and small, should these animals be pets? How are they bought and where do they end up? Carte Blanche investigates.

Summary:
A two year investigation into exotic animals as pets. We have TONS of undercover footage of pet shops, zoos and animal parks. The subsections of animals we will look at: BIG CATS, REPTILES + FISH + BIRDS, MONKEY + OTHERS.
We will look at their rights as exotics verse the rights of local animals in South Africa, but also provincially. We will also look at how they are sold - through breeders - and where they end up -animal testing? hunted/ put down? Rescue centre's?

Further information:
Conservationists are a different breed - so we really need to adhere to the scale - from BAN (BAN ANIMAL TRADING) Who completely believe animals should not be traded. So the NSPCA (who believe wild animals is a business, but would put them down as it's kinder than putting them in a centre). AND EWT - They are pro-trade of animals, see them as a business, but want to do it humanely.

We would also need to speak to those who have wild animals as pets - and why they have them. We would need to look at the laws surrounding trade and why an exotic is so easily available, but a local animal is completely protected. Rod owns several local and exotic animals - and is willing to explain why he has them and how well they are treated. Jugo Maro also has "rescue" animals" but have a "predator park" that was recently liquidated. Both are willing to speak.

There is also the fact that OLX AND GUMTREE have now band the selling of all exotic animals on their pages - which we were able to do two years ago...

Press Release:


Exotic Pets
Fancy a pet tiger? Planning to keep it in your home or backyard? Owning an exotic pet is perfectly legal in South Africa and permits are easy to obtain. But should they be? And, with every province governed by different laws, protecting exotic animals has become a nightmare for animal rights groups. Carte Blanche investigates the trade in these sought-after animals.



Script:


LINK: THIS IS TINKER BELL – SHE’S THREE YEARS OLD, THE BIG QUESTION IS - SHOULD WILD ANIMALS BE PETS?
Tinkerbell is a Caracal and being an indigenous wild animal she’s protected by our laws. It’s not often that permits are granted to keep them as pets.
However, animals like Bengal tigers are exotic. And, a loophole in our law makes it perfectly legal to own them as pets.
Panjo and his owner Goosey Fernandes made world headlines in 2010 when Panjo escaped and roamed the Mpumalanga suburbs until he was found four days later...
Goosey: “Panjo came and he put his head on my shoulders and here, and kissed me and said thanks for finding me.”
Goosey owns a sanctuary for his 22 big cats. After Panjo shot to fame, Goosey got many calls to take in distressed animals like Alex, whose mother rejected her.
Last year, Kujo came to Goosey with torn ears and a broken paw. Kujo’s luckier than his brother, whose body was found in a Benoni driveway.
Goosey: “They said they always took his ears and pinched them to try and teach him. Cos that’s how we teach tigers and lions.”
Meet CC -a 6-month old tiger cub living in a Boksburg backyard - legally. In August concerned neighbours complained to the SPCA. Her owner, Jean Anderson was soon at the centre of a social media war.
Jean: “This woman put my house address online, I have people coming to my house and its unfair. I love this animal and I’ve had her since she was 9 days old.”
He declined an interview, but met with animal rights activist Smaragda Louw.
Smaragda: “I think that jean is a person who got caught up in the fantasy of owning an exotic cat.”
She’s a founder of Ban Animal Trading or “BAT,” a non-profit organization that believes wild animals should be free.
Smaragda: “We take them from their environment. We captive breed them, we hand raise them, we tame them, and then we believe they’re domesticated.”
Goosey admits Panjo’s big adventure sparked a dangerous trend.
Ainsley: “We’ve seen an incline of tigers since Panjo.”
The NSPCA’s Veterinary nurse Ainsley Hay questions whether people like Goosey and Jean - mechanics by trade - have the expertise to care for wild animals. She frequently sees the consequences of ignorance - such as recent case in which two tigers were declawed by their owner.
Ainsley: “It’s actually surgically removing the first digit of their finger and they get very bad arthritis.”
LINK: IN A TWO YEAR INVESTIGATION LOOKING AT THE WILD ANIMAL PET TRADE, WE SPOKE WITH CONSERVATIONISTS, GOVERNMENT, ZOOS AND PET SHOPS.
Ainsley: “South Africa is the hub for legal and illegal trade, because it’s so easy to launder animals.”
The illegal trade in animals is the third largest illicit business globally - after drugs and weapons. And,within our borders, the breeding and sale of animals into the pet trade is largely unregulated.
Ainsley: 28.13 “The provinces all have a department of environmental affairs, they hand out permits like candy to kids. You want to get a zoo, sure fine.”
Smaragda says owner of Gauteng-based Endofaun Zoo - Jimmy Magill - advertised animals to buy and sell online . He also owns a live animal supply business and in 2010 exported 6 Rhino to two zoos in Vietnam and China.
Smaragda: “I don’t see any educational tours for kids happening there. What I see, is a front for trading.”
The NSPCA investigated and found animals housed in “shocking conditions.” Faecal matter was piled high” and “the animals showed obvious signs of illness, mange, untreated injuries, tumours and had breathing difficulties.” They confiscated rodents and snakes and laid charges of animal cruelty.
Smaragda: “Some of the animals were in utterly horrendous condition. I walked into a house basically. There were I don’t know how many cages with marmoset monkeys, with genets, with snakes, birds. And in the same place, they were actually preparing the food for the animals, so there was the smell of rotten chicken.”
Jimmy declined an interview, as the matter is before court. He denies all allegations, and said in writing he is pursuing a civil claim against the NSPCA, for their “flagrant abuse of power” and for “wrongful and malicious prosecution ”
Keith: “Unless a complaint comes in from the public, it’s extremely difficult to monitor it.”
The Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries is responsible for the health and welfare of wild animals. Their veterinary scientist Keith Ramsay says the laws differ provincially and they need to work with the Department of Environment to close any loopholes.
Keith: “One of our concerns with Wild Animals, is are they able to express animal behaviour, are the enclosures that they’re kept in big enough? These animals all have specific needs, and if you don’t feed the animal the right kind of food, you are being cruel.”
Keith says the plan is to draft an animal welfare act.
Keith: “So that you have a proactive approach to animal welfare, where, as an owner of an animal, you would have a legal responsibility to look after that animal.”
Goosey: “Please don’t buy these animals... they cannot live in the back garden of somebody. It’s a dangerous cat and it can hurt people.”
Kelly: “If you can put a cheetah on the front seat of your big flashy car, you’re even more flashy. “
Kelly Marnewick (MARN-A-WICK) manages the endangered wildlife programme for EWT or the Endangered Wild Life Trust – a pro-trade organization that believes in the legal, but ethical trade in animals.
Kelly: “If we are going to be trading in wildlife, it should be sustainable and it should support the conservation of the species in the wild.”
EWT acknowledges that tourism and hunting bring in big bucks. 6.2 billion rand a year according to the Department of Environment.
Kelly: “An example would be maybe trophy hunting which is a controversial one, but if trophy hunting is done correctly, it doesn’t impact on the survival of the species in the wild.”
However, the EWT believes the pet trade exploits exotic animals.
Kelly: “We shouldn’t be appreciating it by cuddling it.”
Goosey does not breed his animals and says breeders often sell a false idea that wild animals make great pets.
Goosey: “They’re just there to breed and make money and sell, they don’t give people the knowledge of how to look after cats, how to ween them, or take them to the toilet.”
Traders are notoriously secretive as their animals can be worth millions, which is why “Craig,” requested anonymity.
He’s had monkeys like “Mike” since he was 16. Mike’s original owner didn’t do his research and when Mike began biting – something expected of a frustrated sexually mature Capuchin Monkey - he gave Mike to Craig.
Craig: “This monkey is hand reared, I’ve tried to introduce him to his own kind, and they bite him.”
Craig says he only breeds endangered wildlife species, and doesn’t sell them.
Craig: “The industry is a monster, and the more rare the animals, the more that they cost. As a private breeder, you need knew blood, so you can swop the female out for someone else’s new blood and you can carry on breeding, adding to the species.”
Craig says proper care for exotic animals is expensive.
Craig: “I’ve just got nice big cages, and it’s clean. They’ve all got specialized diets. I would suppose my cost of running it is 20/25 thousand a month. (monkey sneezing) It’s a personal... bless you, bless you... but it’s a personal thing.”
Goosey’s raw meat bills can reach R27000 a month.
Kelly: “You don’t think about this tiger living in a fancy mansion in a posh area being fed fillet steak as being problematic.”
Craig argues that exotics are valued more highly by their owners than cats or dogs as they are more expensive to acquire.
Craig: “Everybody has a monetary thing to everything. I think most people will disagree with me, but the reality is ITS THERE.”
LINK: BUT WHERE DO WILD ANIMALS, ESPECIALLY EXOTICS, GO WHEN THEY BECOME TOO AGGRESSIVE TO HANDLE, OR TOO EXPENSIVE TO KEEP?
With few sanctuaries for exotic animals, Ainsley says euthanasia is often the only option.
Ainsley: “As horrible as it is to say this, there’s a fate far worse than death.”
Devi: “That’s the psychology? Me me me.”
Smaragda: “That’s the psychology, it’s all about humans and therefore above the animals.”
Ainsley: “If you have to stick something in cage to keep it in your house, it shouldn’t be there.”
The EWT insists we need to question our laws.
Kelly: “They’re not breaking the law, but just because something’s legal, doesn’t mean it’s right. Is it ethical and is it moral?

The subsections of animals we will look at: BIG CATS, REPTILES + FISH + BIRDS, MONKEY + OTHERS. We will look at their rights as exotics verse the rights of local animals in South Africa, but also provincially. We will also look at how they are sold - through breeders - and where they end up -animal testing? hunted/ put down? Rescue centre's?
metadata.Further information: Conservationists are a different breed - so we really need to adhere to the scale - from BAN (BAN ANIMAL TRADING) Who completely believe animals should not be traded. So the NSPCA (who believe wild animals is a business, but would put them down as it's kinder than putting them in a centre). AND EWT - They are pro-trade of animals, see them as a business, but want to do it humanely. We would also need to speak to those who have wild animals as pets - and why they have them. We would need to look at the laws surrounding trade and why an exotic is so easily available, but a local animal is completely protected. Rod owns several local and exotic animals - and is willing to explain why he has them and how well they are treated. Jugo Maro also has "rescue" animals" but have a "predator park" that was recently liquidated. Both are willing to speak. There is also the fact that OLX AND GUMTREE have now band the selling of all exotic animals on their pages - which we were able to do two years ago...
